title: Restriction of a locally quasi-finite morphism to open subschemes is locally quasi-finite (Stacks 01TH (4))
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq S$ be open subschemes with $f(U)\subseteq V$, with inclusions $\iota_U:U\to X$, $\iota_V:V\to S$ (open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]), and let $f|_U:U\to V$ be the unique morphism with $\iota_V\circ f|_U=f\circ\iota_U$. Then $f|_U:U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH, part (4): quasi-finiteness at a point may be checked on any pair of affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $f(\operatorname{Spec}A)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing the point; this is the 'local nature of local quasi-finiteness' invoked in the proof of Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03JA.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, part (4) and its proof; Definition Tag 01TD (definition-quasi-finite), line 3538; as invoked in the proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, line 15495

proof.text: Apply locallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite to f and hf. The Mathlib instance instLocallyOfFiniteTypeResLE supplies LocallyOfFiniteType (f.resLE V U e).

source.place: Remark following Definition Tag 01TD; finite type is local on source and target.

proof.text: For x in the open subscheme U, apply quasiFiniteAtPoint_isolated_in_fiber to f at U.ι x using hf (U.ι x). Its first component is isolation in the scheme-theoretic fibre. Apply Mathlib Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber.mpr to obtain f.QuasiFiniteAt (U.ι x). The finite-type instance from step 1 is required here.

The restriction square resLE_comp_ι says f.resLE V U e ≫ V.ι = U.ι ≫ f. Rewriting with Mathlib Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_comp_iff (g := V.ι) and quasiFiniteAt_comp_iff_of_isOpenImmersion transfers f.QuasiFiniteAt (U.ι x) to (f.resLE V U e).QuasiFiniteAt x. Apply quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber.mp for the restricted locally finite type morphism to recover isolation in its fibre. Both inclusions are open immersions; the target inclusion is therefore Mathlib LocallyQuasiFinite.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01TH: isolation is unchanged by restriction to open subschemes; implemented by the cited proved Mathlib stalk-map criteria.

proof.text: Inside the target open subscheme V choose an affine open V′ containing (f.resLE V U e) x by Mathlib exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset applied to the top open. Inside the source open subscheme U choose an affine open U′ containing x and contained in the inverse image of V′ by a second application. Apply isQuasiFiniteAtPrime_of_isOpen_singleton_asFiber to f.resLE V U e, its isolated fibre point from step 3, and U′, V′. The output is the finite-type witness together with Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime for its induced map on sections.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01TH, (2) implies (4); Schemes Tag 01IT for the affine neighbourhoods.

proof.text: The opens U′ and V′, their affine proofs, membership of x, the containment U′ ≤ (f.resLE V U e)⁻¹(V′), and the ring-theoretic witness of step 4 are precisely the existential fields of IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint (f.resLE V U e) x. Abstract over arbitrary x to obtain IsLocallyQuasiFinite (f.resLE V U e).

proof_origin.place: Tags 01TD and 01TH, (1) implies (2) implies (4), with Schemes Tag 01IT. C2 assembles the existing project lemmas using proved Mathlib pointwise stalk-map criteria to transport isolation across the restriction square, and applies the affine-pair theorem directly to the restricted morphism. split_report.summary: Read pqf-def-quasifinite: it takes the affine-local ring-theoretic definition of Stacks 01TD (1) (an affine pair Spec A ∋ x, Spec R with R -> A of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of x), so the pair the definition gives need not lie in U, V and the proof must change the pair: that is Stacks 01TH, (1) => (2) => (4). Statement kept (checked against 01TD and 01TH (4)); stmt_deps kept. Proof in five steps: f is locally of finite type (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type, the 'trivially' remark after 01TD, which rests on 01T2); choice of affine opens u ∈ U' ⊆ U ∩ f^{-1}(V'), s ∈ V' ⊆ V (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis, Stacks 01IT, Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens); u isolated in X_s by the existing lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated (01TH (1)=>(2)) and then R' -> A' of finite type and quasi-finite at q' by the new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs (01TH (2)=>(4), where 'isolated in X_s stays isolated in U_s' and U_s = Spec(A ⊗ κ(p)) belong); the ring map of f|_U on (U',V') is that of f (open subscheme structure sheaves are restrictions), giving quasi-finiteness of f|_U at u by 01TD (1). This route makes the fibre of f|_U unnecessary (only fibres of f occur). Mathlib: Mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite (QuasiFinite.lean:71) omits locally of finite type, so the resLE instance (:132) is a candidate only, re-checked by sed. Searched the DAG for 01IT, 01T2, 01TH, 'isolated'/'quasi-finite at', 'locally quasi-finite'+'locally of finite type' before creating the three nodes.

reviewed.note: 5 steps from the definition 01TD (1) via Stacks 01TH (1)=>(2)=>(4): locally quasi-finite implies locally of finite type (new unsplit node, remark after 01TD); affine opens inside U and V around the point (new 01IT leaf, AffineScheme.lean:305 verified by L); the point is isolated in its fibre (existing node) and then quasi-finite on any affine pair (new unsplit 01TH (2)=>(4) node, Mathlib candidate recorded since Mathlib's QuasiFiniteAt is defined differently); the pair is the same for f|_U; conclusion. Mathlib's resLE instance for LocallyQuasiFinite is not a leaf because that class omits locally of finite type.
